info.desc: Filth is the debut studio album by American experimental rock band Swans. Only band leader and vocalist Michael Gira and drummer Jonathan Kane remained from the original lineup of the band. Filth is the first Swans release to feature the experimental and noisy playing style that the band's early work would become known for. The album's distinct sound is partly the product of a new lineup featuring two drummers (Roli Mosimann and Kane). It also marks the first appearance of future Swans regular Norman Westberg. podcast.body: Released early in the band's career, this album, along with *Cop*, is today considered a true gem and a masterpiece of guitar sound experimentation. At the time of its release, Michael Gira was not a professional musician and had another job. It was released on independent labels and received little to no repercussion, selling very few copies and failing to gain recognition, making it difficult for the band to secure concerts. Critics gave it very bad reviews, finding it radically different from the mass-consumed rock of the early 80s by bands like Metallica and Iron Maiden. Its sound was completely atmospheric, contrasting with the sharp, virtuoso, and fast guitar playing common in 80s rock. The lyrics, penned by Michael Gira, were disturbing, addressing themes such as sex, religion, cruelty, submission (sometimes voluntary), love leading to submission, vile behaviors, and aggression. These lyrics were so powerful that, had the band been famous, they likely would have been censored. "Hoy en día esos dos trabajos están considerados, obras maestras de la experimentación del sonido de guitarra."

podcast.body: This album, released in 1983, showcased a very dense and distorted guitar sound, aligning with a broader trend in music towards heavier sonic textures during that year. Its simultaneous release with R.E.M.'s *Murmur* illustrates the stark contrasts in guitar aesthetics present in the early 1980s. "sale el primer disco de Swans, el fifth."
